title: GH#33754: fix(pulse): keep CPU admission open for idle-core headroom when load average is I/O-inflated
body:
## Summary

Pulse's CPU admission gate closed on the one-minute load average alone. On 2026-10-06 load reached 147/16 cores while `top` showed about 37% CPU idle and macOS memory pressure was normal. A Backblaze rescan and Brave renderers had inflated load with blocked threads, and the gate set max workers to 0. The intent, confirmed by the maintainer, is to keep progressing with whatever resources are actually free.

- `_pulse_cpu_pressure` (`.agents/scripts/pulse-capacity.sh`) now samples CPU idle only when load would close the gate. It uses macOS `iostat -n 0 -c 2 -w 1` (about 1s wall, negligible CPU, unlike `top -l 1` which costs about 1.6s of system CPU on this host) or a Linux `/proc/stat` delta that counts idle only, so iowait-bound hosts stay closed. If idle is at least `orchestration.cpu_idle_admit_percent` (default 25, 0 disables), the gate becomes `open_idle`. The output gains a fifth `idle|na` field.
- `pulse_apply_provider_load_capacity_cap` limits `open_idle` passes to `active + floor(cores × idle% / 100)` (at least 1 new worker). The next pass re-samples, so admission tracks real headroom. The preflight RAM target is unchanged in `open_idle`, and `closed` still writes 0.
- The capacity log lines now include `cpu_idle_pct`. `open_idle` passes log `idle_slots` with `admission=idle_headroom`.
- The new config key is added to the defaults, the schema, the `config-helper.sh` env mapping (`AIDEVOPS_CPU_IDLE_ADMIT_PERCENT`), `pulse-wrapper-config.sh` and `reference/configuration.md`.

## Verification

- `shellcheck` clean on all changed scripts.
- `test-pulse-cpu-admission.sh`: 44 assertions pass, using the existing OS-telemetry stub pattern extended with `iostat` and `/proc/stat` stubs. Cases cover Darwin and Linux: idle above, equal to and below the threshold, 0 disables, invalid value falls back to 25, missing idle telemetry stays closed, idle-headroom cap `13 0` for 7 active on 16 cores at 40% idle, the floor stays within headroom, and the env mapping.
- These suites also pass: `test-config-schema-defaults`, `test-dispatch-min-concurrency`, `test-pulse-wrapper-worker-count`, `test-dispatch-max-parallel`, `test-config-helper-tmp-home`, `test-pulse-wrapper-characterization`.
- Real host telemetry: idle sampled at 46%. A forced high-load reading gives `37.01 16 open_idle 0.1 46`; a threshold of 100 gives `closed`; the default path gives `37.01 16 open 4.0 na` with no sampling cost.

Resolves #33754

- **Risk level:** medium
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — source the production capacity/preflight/refill helpers with controlled OS/provider telemetry, plus live process detection on this shared host; no actual worker dispatch or host load generation.
- `shellcheck -x` and `bash -n` pass for all four changed shell files.

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-current-state-guardrails.sh`: 27 tests, zero failures. Its isolated fixture emits an existing missing-default-config diagnostic while still passing.
- Live detector reports two users. Five direct function timings: 78, 76, 94, 88 and 92 ms. Standalone bash-launch benchmarks also include process startup/scheduling and reached 127 ms; the timed detector invocation itself is the cycle-cost evidence. Timing is host/load-dependent, not a hard real-time guarantee.
- Bash 3.2 compatibility checked by construct review: indexed arrays, `[[ ]]`, arithmetic and here-strings only; no associative arrays, `mapfile` or newer Bash features. An actual Bash 3.2 executable/macOS host was not available.
- Direct `shfmt -d` reports existing formatting differences outside the implementation sections; no unrelated reformatting is included. ShellCheck and commit/push hooks pass.
- Repaired the terminal Complexity Analysis failure at the first ready head by extracting the shared-host clamp; `.agents/scripts/complexity-regression-helper.sh check --base 6af75a08e9ff6c6817949a08b8746a2677acbb3d --head HEAD` now reports base 0, head 0, new 0 violations. CPU-admission verification and scoped ShellCheck were rerun after the repair.

## Acceptance review (self-review)

| Criterion | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Two active runner users split the automatic worker target and log the count | Production helpers tested with two UIDs: ceiling 12 becomes 6 in preflight and refill on both OS telemetry paths; log assertion binds `colocated_runners=2 shared_host_worker_cap=6 worker_cap_auto=1`. Live detector also reports 2. |
| Explicit override remains per-runner | Explicit ceiling 12 remains 12 with three users; positive config/environment cap provenance is preserved at wrapper initialization. |
| Single-runner CPU policy unchanged | Existing full-use 4.0 threshold, closed-gate, idle-headroom, provider and minimum-floor regression suites pass. CPU-pressure helper is unchanged. |
| ShellCheck clean, compatible implementation, lightweight detection | Scoped ShellCheck/syntax checks pass; compatibility reviewed as above; direct live detector samples are 76–94 ms. |

Review bundle SHA-256: `74ade4db9f1b11c7541131ffd3e9de414a25a92a8d4b671a418d584ab0eba91f`, head `88e68e3aceaa547cfd4863b07e5e7dc9b2e94541`; prompt-injection scan clean. All branch commits and the complete diff were inspected directly, including the behavior-preserving complexity repair.

Keep the default load gate at 4.0 rather than changing existing full-CPU admission. Divide the automatic ceiling only; explicit per-user budgets remain authoritative. The detector uses numeric UIDs, avoids shared writable host registries, and refreshes on preflight/refill. title: Chore(deps): bump hono from 4.13.8 to 4.13.11
body:
Bumps [hono](https://github.com/honojs/hono) from 4.13.8 to 4.13.11.
Release notes

Sourced from hono's releases.

v4.13.11

Security fixes

serveStatic decodes the request path a second time, leading to bypass of middleware on static paths

Affects: hono/serve-static and the adapters built on it (hono/bun, hono/deno, hono/cloudflare-workers, @hono/bun, @hono/deno, @hono/cloudflare-workers). Fixes serveStatic decoding an already-decoded path, where a crafted request could be routed as one path and served as another, skipping middleware mounted on a static prefix. GHSA-5r4p-p66f-jhc7

serveStatic now rejects request paths that still contain % after decoding. To serve files whose names contain a literal %, set allowPercentInPath: true.

The same fix ships in @hono/node-server v2.1.3.

v4.13.10

Adapters are now separate packages

The runtime adapters are now published as their own packages: @hono/bun, @hono/deno, @hono/cloudflare-workers, @hono/aws-lambda, @hono/lambda-edge, @hono/netlify, @hono/vercel, and @hono/service-worker. @hono/deno is also on JSR.

hono/<adapter> still works in v4 but is deprecated and will be removed in v5. Migrating is an import change:

- import { serveStatic } from 'hono/bun'
+ import { serveStatic } from '@hono/bun'

hono/cloudflare-pages is deprecated without a replacement package; Cloudflare recommends Workers with static assets.

title: t18595: fix(pulse): bound repeated CI-drift rebases (GH#33794)
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33794. Prevent repeated CI-drift rebases when the same required contexts fail on a new head after one successful refresh.

- Add a runner-local atomic TSV ledger keyed by repository/PR, failing-context signature and pre-rebase head, with seven-day expiry and pruning.
- Expose sorted terminal failed required-context names using the existing exact-head REST classification pattern.
- Consult and record the ledger in `_pmp_stage_required_checks`; repeated failures route to the existing CI fix-worker. Preserve pending-check and dry-run fences, unknown-state fail-open behavior, and strict review-repair semantics.
- Extend the existing routing suite with signature, head, expiry, corrupt-state, pending, dry-run, and classification cases.

## Files and reference pattern

Only `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-ci-drift-ledger.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge.sh`, `.agents/scripts/pulse-merge-required-checks.sh`, and `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh` change. Classification mirrors `_check_required_checks_has_terminal_failure`; the rebase implementation and dispatch internals remain unchanged.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: high; runtime-verified. Implementation head: `d927df33a5b518d454214919e840eaa29729759e`.

- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-ci-repair-routing.sh`: 56/56 pass.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-update-branch.sh`: 17/17 pass.
- `bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-routine-standalone.sh`: 25/25 pass.
- ShellCheck on all four changed files: clean.
- `.agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed`: passes, including Bash 3.2 compatibility, function complexity, nesting, portability, and secrets checks.

### Pre-existing verification exception

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh`: 24 cases, 11 failures caused by `_route_pr_resolve_work_issue: command not found`. Reproduced exactly against an isolated `git archive a15f1aada` baseline. `git diff --exit-code a15f1aada -- .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-merge-pr-context.sh .agents/scripts/pulse-merge-process.sh` passes: neither its test nor implementation was changed by this PR. Its six CI-rebase/review-repair cases pass. Per the first-pass contract, unrelated harness repairs are not included.

The remaining advisory shfmt differences in `pulse-merge.sh` and the routing suite also exist in the archived base (`shfmt -l` reports both). Added code is formatted; the new ledger is shfmt-clean. The required-checks library has one pre-existing repeated `commit_status` literal warning. No new quality regressions remain.

## Decisions and review

Signatures use SHA-256 of sorted unique terminal-failed required names. Ledger writes are runner-local, atomic, replace one PR entry, and prune expired state. Pending checks are fenced before using historical ledger evidence, including when a terminal failure coexists with active checks. Unknown classification retains the existing rebase behavior and logs its unavailable evidence. Direct diff inspection plus a bounded advisory review found no concrete production defects. Review-repair, rebase semantics, and fix-worker internals remain unchanged.

title: GH#33887: fix NixOS-safe OpenCode shim generation
body:
## Summary

Resolves #33887. Fix the setup generator in `.agents/scripts/setup/modules/tool-install.sh`, with focused coverage in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh`.

- Discover Nix user/system profiles and preserve logical profile paths across upgrades and garbage collection.
- Reject managed launcher cycles and self-target aliases before execution; retain bounded runtime probes for other candidates.
- Escape generated target/PATH literals and validate the temporary launcher before replacing an existing launcher.

## Root cause and decisions

The old generator validated a logical candidate, then used `pwd -P` on its directory to construct a different execution target without validating that rewritten target before installation. That permits directory-symlink collapse and pins Nix store generations. Discovery omitted Nix profile paths and skipped only textual self-target matches. The reported `/bin/opencode` target is confirmed by the issue, but the precise historical symlink topology and claimed recursion are not verified; this change does not invent that evidence. Stable profile symlinks are preferred to immutable store pins so Nix upgrades and GC can advance the executable.

## Runtime Testing

Risk: medium. Local simulated Nix profile coverage runs the generated launcher in a clean `env -i` environment. No authorized NixOS host is available; this is not actual NixOS runtime evidence.

- ShellCheck 0.9.0 passes on both changed shell files.
- New 16 focused regression assertions pass (legacy/modern profiles, later store PATH entries, upgrades/GC simulation, aliases/cycles, quoting, argument boundaries, exit status, missing target, failed generated-launcher preservation).

```bash
command() {
    if [[ "${1:-}" == "-v" ]]; then
        local resolved=""
        resolved=$(builtin command -v "${2:-}") || return 1
        case "$resolved" in /bin/opencode | /usr/bin/opencode) return 1 ;; esac
    fi
    builtin command "$@"
    return $?
}
export -f command
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-tool-install-opencode.sh
```

title: GH#33890: fix finalize-receipt marker retirement for merge-cleanup aliases
body:
## Summary

Marker retirement in finalize-receipt reused the strict adoption resolver (#28915), which requires the local branch to equal the PR head ref. Merge cleanup, however, records a same-repository alias (a local repair branch at the exact PR head, delete_remote_branch=0). So finalize-receipt marked the receipt COMPLETE and then refused to retire the alias marker, leaving the worktree dirty. The resolver core is now _merge_fresh_merged_worktree_cleanup_target with an adopt or retire mode. _merge_fresh_adopted_worktree_cleanup_target stays strict, including its 1/2/3 return codes. The new _merge_fresh_retirement_worktree_cleanup_target also accepts the alias that _merge_current_worktree_cleanup_target already proves: exact head OID, registered linked-worktree record, same head repository and GitHub repository identity. Retirement still holds the receipt lock and requires the finalized receipt to record that exact worktree and branch, along with owner session, PID, process generation, pending lease, untracked non-symlink marker and exact marker contents. Because finalization is idempotent, rerunning finalize-receipt retires markers already stuck in the partial state.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-merge-cleanup.sh, .agents/scripts/full-loop-helper-state-lifecycle.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh

## Runtime Testing

- **Risk level:** Critical
- **Verification:** runtime-verified — Runtime: used live GitHub metadata for merged PR #33900. A linked alias worktree (local branch local/alias-repair-33900 at the exact merged head b308a256) was created in a sandbox repo, with receipts and registry sandboxed. Merge cleanup's own recorder wrote the deferred receipt and marker, then the real CLIs ran: record-no-release, then finalize-receipt. Base main: finalize-receipt rc=1 'legacy cleanup marker does not match', receipt COMPLETE, marker present, worktree dirty ('?? .agents/.full-loop-cleanup-deferred'). This branch: rc=0, marker removed, receipt branch=local/alias-repair-33900 COMPLETE/CLEANUP_DEFERRED, worktree clean. Tests: test-full-loop-cleanup-receipt.sh all pass, including 2 new GH#33890 blocks. Those blocks check: adoption still rejects the renamed branch; the retirement resolver returns the alias with delete_remote_branch=0; a receipt recording another branch keeps the marker; a cross-repository head keeps the marker; a retry from the stuck state retires the marker; a second run is idempotent. The existing GH#33627 negatives (pending, missing, malformed, mismatched, symlink, PID reuse, lease) still pass. test-full-loop-merge-worktree-cleanup.sh: 27/27. shellcheck is clean. Fixture fix: TEST_ROOT is canonicalized with pwd -P. On macOS, mktemp returns /var/... but git reports /private/var/..., so the existing GH#33627 block failed on unmodified main on macOS. Production records both sides from git rev-parse.

Resolves #33890

title: GH#33881: fix blocked-by value grammar to ignore negation-led values and trailing prose
body:
## Summary

Three parsers extracted every ID from free text after a Blocked by label: the pulse-dep-graph.sh bash path, the production pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq reducer, and dependency-event-reconciler.sh _der_dependency_text. So 'Blocked by: nothing ... (t139–t149)' and 'none (t136 and t138 merged)' produced false edges that blocked dispatch. All three now share one value grammar: the new blocked-by-value.awk, used by both bash paths, and a jq twin, blocker_value_line. Negation-led values (none, nothing, no, n/a, nil, a dash) yield no references. A leading reference list keeps only #N, GH#N, owner/repo#N, 'owner/repo #N' and task-ID-shaped tokens, separated by commas, whitespace, ';', 'and', '&', '+' or '/', and stops at the first prose token. Backticks, emphasis and trailing punctuation are ignored. A prose-led value keeps legacy whole-line extraction, so an ambiguous declaration fails closed instead of losing a real blocker. Invalid task-ID-shaped tokens inside a list are kept, so __malformed__ still fires. The output is still a field line, so re-parsing is idempotent. If the grammar file is missing, extraction falls back to whole-line.



## Files Changed

.agents/scripts/blocked-by-value.awk, .agents/scripts/dependency-event-reconciler.sh, .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph-reduce.jq, .agents/scripts/pulse-dep-graph.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-event-reconciler.sh, .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dep-graph-prose-dependencies.sh

title: fix(pulse): distinguish incomplete queue scans from GitHub failures
body:
## Summary

Distinguish incomplete diagnostic collection from GitHub failures in the bounded pulse queue scanner.

- Check dependency eligibility across repository inventories before spending remaining time on optional durable-progress history.
- Preserve unknown dependencies and fail-closed availability after deadline exhaustion, without counting uncollected evidence as a GitHub error.
- Record truncated repository inventories separately and expose `queue_inventory_truncated` when collection otherwise finishes within budget.
- Extend the existing diagnostic regression suite for deadline and truncation classification; actual API failures still produce the existing error finding.

## Evidence

A read-only diagnostic run previously counted deadline-limited dependency checks and the configured inventory limit as GitHub errors. A live run using this patch reported `gh_errors=0`, `repos_truncated=1`, and `queue_budget_exhausted`, retaining honest partial-observation semantics rather than claiming a complete queue scan.

This changes diagnostic accounting only. It does not change worker permissions, ownership, launch admission, dispatch concurrency, API limits, or catalogue publication.

## Files and reference pattern

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-check-queue-scan.py`: retain cached bounded inventories, the existing global deadline, and conservative dependency handling.
- `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-check-helper.sh`: reuse the existing slow-dependency, truncation, and real-API-error fixtures.

title: fix(pulse): preserve configured toolchain PATH precedence
body:
## Summary

- Preserve the operator's configured toolchain precedence when normalizing Pulse's PATH.
- Append existing platform fallback directories instead of prepending them; retain the guarded Linuxbrew fallback and support an unset or empty PATH without adding an empty search entry.
- Scope the implementation to `.agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh`, with focused coverage in `.agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-path-precedence.sh`; no scheduler, task ownership, credential, or dispatch policy changes.

## Evidence and rationale

A Linux runner repeatedly failed to execute the resolved `/bin/jq` with `Permission denied`. JSON configuration and health-state processing then failed, producing misleading empty-repository observations. The same host's setup also resolved npm through an unusable `/usr/bin/npm` entry and failed with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

The configured Nix toolchain successfully executes both tools. Prepending conventional filesystem directories displaced that working configuration. After deploying this change through scoped setup, Pulse writes its health state again, detects the configured repositories and provider account, and reports a current runtime. A new enrichment launch after this repair is not claimed.

The existing platform fallback list is the reference pattern: keep its contents and Linuxbrew guard, changing only precedence. Homebrew fallback directories remain available on macOS. An actual macOS runtime test was not performed.

## Regression Evidence

`bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-path-precedence.sh` exercises the actual bootstrap PATH block without starting Pulse or contacting GitHub. Six cases cover Darwin and Linux with a configured, empty, or unset PATH. It requires the operator's configured directories to stay first, verifies all existing platform fallback directories remain available, and rejects empty PATH entries. The previous prepend expression fails the configured-PATH assertion. The test uses isolated child shells with a mocked platform probe; this is branch-behavior coverage, not a claim of a physical macOS runtime test.

## Verification

- `bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main` — passed (native Secretlint unavailable during this run; its broad scan remains delegated to CI).
- `shellcheck .agents/scripts/pulse-wrapper.sh` — passed.

- Local scoped setup — passed with the working system toolchain first in PATH; the fresh Pulse process writes `pulse-health.json` and no new bundle-specific `jq: Permission denied` errors were observed in the bounded verification window.

## Scope and delivery

Only the bootstrap PATH expression, its explanatory comment, and the focused regression test change. No release or merge is requested by this PR. The local installation currently includes this fix; upstream review and merge are needed to preserve it across future updates.

title: fix(pulse): defer backlog normalization during post-label refill
body:
## Summary

- Keep the post-label fast refill off the synchronous full-backlog dependency-normalization path by using the existing `skip` mode, as the first wave already does.
- Keep blocked issues filtered and preserve every live per-candidate dependency, trust, capability, claim, footprint and timeout gate. Existing housekeeping and normal sweeps retain normalization.
- Do not lend reserved product slots on a deferred-readiness snapshot containing blocked work; a complete transport response is not proof of complete dependency discovery.

Resolves #33944

## Observed regression

On the merged PATH repair from #33934, an initial worker launched successfully. However, the subsequent post-label refill took **936 seconds**, processed only **5/118** candidates, launched **0** product workers and stopped when its remaining budget fell below the per-candidate floor. Worker-exit refills encountered the still-owned cycle lock. Label maintenance itself took only 76 seconds.

## Implementation / review scope

- `.agents/scripts/pulse-dispatch-preflight-lib.sh`: invalidate the candidate snapshot as before, then refill with `apply_dispatch_max "skip"`. This remains a full repository scan, not the partial first-wave mode.
- `.agents/scripts/pulse-repo-meta.sh`: recognize blocked readiness consistently for GitHub and normalized label shapes; conservatively retain incomplete product-discovery evidence when normalization is deferred.
- Existing first-wave and dependency-readiness suites cover the fast refill, preserved blocked filtering, retained available candidates, reserved capacity and normal normalization recovery.

Trade-off: a blocked child that becomes dependency-ready is exposed by the existing normalization/housekeeping paths rather than delaying every already-available candidate in this fast refill. No scheduler, test runner or deployment infrastructure is added.

## Regression Evidence

Passed locally:

```bash
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-dependency-readiness-normalization.sh  # 65 passed, 0 failed
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-first-wave.sh
bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-dispatch-candidate-snapshot.sh

bash .agents/scripts/tests/test-pulse-event-refill.sh                 # 29 passed, 0 failed
bash .agents/scripts/linters-local.sh --changed --base-ref origin/main
bun run typecheck
```

The readiness suite initially failed on the untouched base too: its "partial native repair" fixture returned native status **2**, meaning positively clear, but expected declared-edge fallback. The fixture now uses status **1**, meaning absent native relationships, and separately verifies that status **2** remains authoritative. Production native dependency semantics are unchanged.

Local ShellCheck, secretlint, whitespace, Bash 3.2 and complexity regression gates passed. Existing shfmt differences are advisory; unrelated formatting is left unchanged.

This follow-up is not yet deployed, and no new award-enrichment completion is claimed. After approved merge, activate the canonical runtime and inspect a fresh fast refill, actual worker registrations and award-enrichment outcomes separately. No live catalogue publication, permissions change or customer fixture creation is included.

body:
## Summary

Claude Haiku 5.5 (`anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5`) was released on 2026-10-07. It is now the Anthropic `simple`-tier model, replacing Haiku 4.5, and runs at `medium` effort.

- **Routing:** updated `model-routing-table.json`, `aidevops.defaults.jsonc` (tiers and fallback chains), `fallback-chain-config.json.txt`, the `shared-model-tier.sh` fallback list and the helper defaults (`context-budget-helper.sh`, `efficiency-analysis-runner.sh`, `generate-opencode-agents.sh`, `model-registry-helper.sh`, `profile-readme-data-lib.sh`).
- **Pricing:** added a `haiku-5-5` entry ($0.10 in / $0.50 out / $0.01 cache read / $0.125 cache write per 1M tokens) to `model-pricing.json`, `observability-pricing.mjs` and `shared-model-tier.sh`. Pricing version is now `2026-10-07.1`. Prompts over 100K tokens cost 5x; the flat table does not model this, and the source note says so.
- **Sonnet 5.5 correction:** Anthropic's pricing page lists the Sonnet 5.5 cache read at $0.10, not $0.20. Fixed in the pricing table and `models-sonnet.md`.
- **Catalogs:** `model-limits.mjs` (1M context / 128K output), Claude CLI display name in `config-hook.mjs`, proxy alias `haiku` → 5.5 (`haiku45` keeps 4.5). models.dev already lists the model, so no catalog bridge entry is needed.
- **Migration:** `setup/modules/migration-haiku-5-5.sh` is a one-time rewrite of provider-prefixed Haiku 4.5 pins in user settings. It follows the Sonnet 5.5 migration pattern: backups, symlinks skipped, permissions kept, JSON validated, and a retry on failure. `setup.sh` calls it in both interactive and non-interactive setup. Test: `tests/test-haiku-5-5-migration.sh`.
- **Docs:** `models-haiku.md`, `model-routing.md`, `configuration.md`, `context-budget.md`, `auto-reason.md`, `optimize-tiers.md`.

Not in this PR: the direct Messages API helpers (`ai-research-helper.sh`, `verify-operation-helper.sh`) stay on Haiku 4.5. With Haiku 5.5, thinking is on by default and non-default sampling parameters are rejected. Those helpers need parser changes first, tracked in #33967.

## Sources

- Anthropic model overview: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/haiku-5-5/overview
- Anthropic pricing: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing

## Runtime testing

title: GH#33976: fix(pulse): count logical opus workers, not processes, in opus concurrency cap
body:
## Summary

_dispatch_check_model_concurrency_cap counted every process matching `pgrep -f 'opencode.*-m anthropic/claude-opus'`. Each headless worker is a process chain whose argv all carry the inner opencode command: the sandbox-exec-helper.sh wrapper, the opencode launcher and, for npm installs, the native .opencode binary. Inflight was inflated 2-3x, so the default cap of 4 admitted only 1-2 real opus workers. New _dispatch_count_opus_worker_roots reads one `ps axwwo uid=,pid=,ppid=,stat=,command=` snapshot. It keeps processes owned by the effective UID that are not zombie or stopped and that contain an `opencode[N] run ... -m anthropic/claude-opus` invocation, then counts only chain roots: matches whose parent is not itself a match. The probe still fails open (0) when ps or id fails. The dispatch-model-caps.conf comment is synced.



## Files Changed
